data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：对某政治人物及其政策的评价，尤其是关于限制财富积累和亿万富翁税的政策提议，以及这些政策可能带来的社会和经济影响。

不同观点：
• [Aurornis] 认为该政治人物在竞选活动中更多是在重复一些能引起部分选民共鸣的口号，而没有提供具体的政策内容。他指出，记者提出的问题比较简单，让该政治人物有机会发表观点，但仍未涉及任何实际政策。

• [ggm] 认为，限制财富积累的提议在去除政治意图后有一定的合理性，但同时也指出，有些人认为自己有权积累无限财富。他质疑是否有人能够真正创造如此巨大的价值以 justify 亿万富翁的收入，并通过“franking credits”的例子说明即使低收入人群也可能反对限制成为亿万富翁的政策。此外，他还讨论了基金经理的成本和回报问题，认为这进一步挑战了该提议的合理性。

• [hollerith] 以讽刺的语气提问，是否该政治人物也认为纽约市的亿万富翁不应该被允许离开。这个评论暗示了对限制亿万富翁自由流动政策的反对。

• [FridayoLeary] 认为需要对该政治人物进行更多讨论，因为他有可能成为纽约市市长。他警告说，如果不调整其政策，可能会造成经济和社会灾难。评论指出，关键问题不在于亿万富翁与社会其他部分的对立，而在于何种政策能为人们带来最大利益。他还提到，富人可能会因为这些政策离开纽约，导致城市失去税收。

• [billy99k] 以讽刺和挑衅的语气表示，想看看这位“疯狂的社会主义者”如何摧毁纽约市，并将责任归咎于共和党。

• [abbycurtis33] 批评讨论中对基本的供需关系缺乏理解，认为这种无知“令人震惊且悲哀”。

补充讨论：
• 涉及对财富积累限制政策的合理性及其执行难度的争论。
• 讨论了亿万富翁可能因高税收或限制政策而离开城市，对地方经济的影响。
• 提到了社会对“平等”和“社会正义”原则的追求及其潜在负面影响。
• 涉及到对具体经济概念（如基金经理的回报、franking credits）的理解和应用。
• 争议焦点在于财富限制政策的有效性和公平性，以及其对经济和社会的长远影响。

data.title: Companies Should Beware Promoting AI in Products
data.author: mpweiher
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AI应用的优势与用户体验之间的平衡

不同观点：
• **Uehreka的观点**：  
  - 认为AI的优势必须明显且值得，才能证明投资的合理性。  
  - 举例说明ChatGPT在学生和开发者中迅速获得认可，因为它的应用场景直接且有用。  
  - 批评Meta AI的推出失败，认为其UI臃肿且建议的提示不切实际，导致用户体验差。  
  - 虽然看到Meta AI的潜在价值，但质疑用户是否会再给它机会。

• **mpweiher的观点**：  
  - 未详细展开，但通过提供的链接可能暗示对AI相关讨论或资源的兴趣。

• **paulnpace的观点**：  
  - 认为在许多互动中，被迫使用AI的服务体验变差。  
  - 直接表达对当前AI应用在服务中表现的不满，暗示AI的强制使用未必提升用户体验。

补充讨论：
- **用户对AI的第一印象重要性**：Uehreka强调Meta AI因为初次体验差可能失去用户信任，即便后续改进也未必能挽回。
- **AI应用场景的实用性**：Uehreka指出ChatGPT在特定人群中的成功是因为其直接满足了实际需求，如写文章和编码。
- **AI在服务中的强制使用问题**：paulnpace指出AI在某些服务中强制使用，反而导致用户体验下降，这与Uehreka对Meta AI的批评有相似之处。

争议焦点：
- **AI应用的实用性与用户体验之间的矛盾**：一方认为AI需要有明确的实用价值才能被接受，另一方则直接指出当前AI在实际应用中的服务体验存在问题。
- **第一印象与后续改进的关系**：Uehreka认为Meta AI因初次体验差可能失去用户信任，即便后续改进也未必能挽回，这暗示了对AI产品初次体验的高度重视。

data.title: Amber insect fossils reveal "zombie" fungi likely lived alongside dinosaurs
data.author: jackgavigan
data.article_summary: 科学家在9900万年前的琥珀中发现了一只头部被寄生真菌穿出的苍蝇，以及一只感染类似真菌的年轻蚂蚁。这两种真菌属于已灭绝的Ophiocordyceps属，分别命名为Paleoophiocordyceps gerontoformicae和Paleoophiocordyceps ironomyiae。这类“僵尸真菌”通过操控宿主行为来传播，最终致其死亡。研究表明，这种寄生现象在白垩纪时期已经存在，并可能对当时生态系统产生复杂影响。尽管现代此类真菌主要感染蚂蚁，但苍蝇的案例显示出古代寄生多样性。该发现揭示了寄生真菌进化历史的一角。
data.comments_summary:

44391590.article_content:
Fungus can be seen growing out of the head of a fly encased in 99 million-year-old amber.
Nanjing Institute of Geology and Palaeontology; Chinese Academy of Sciences/NIGPAS
Sign up for
CNN’s Wonder Theory science newsletter
. Explore the universe with news on fascinating discoveries, scientific advancements and more.
CNN
—
A glob of 99 million-year-old amber has preserved an ancient fly in horror show fashion: with the mushroom-like fruiting body of zombie fungus bursting forth from its head.
The insect, along with a second specimen of a young ant infected with a similar fungus, are two of the oldest examples of a bizarre natural phenomenon that involves fungal parasites hijacking the bodies of their hosts before ultimately killing them.
“Amber gives us this opportunity to visualize the ancient ecological relationships preserved in fossils,” said Yuhui Zhuang, a doctoral student at the Institute of Paleontology at Yunnan University in southwestern China.
“Overall, these two fossils are very rare, at least among the tens of thousands of amber specimens we’ve seen, and only a few have preserved the symbiotic relationship between fungi and insects,” added Zhuang, the lead author of a
study on the fossils p
ublished June 11 in the journal Proceedings of the Royal Society B: Biological Sciences.
Zhuang and his colleagues named two previously unknown species of ancient fungi of the genus Ophiocordyceps from their research on the amber, which involved using optical microscopes to study the tiny pieces of amber and micro-computed tomography to make 3D images of the fungi-infected insects.
They found the first, named Paleoophiocordyceps gerontoformicae, on the ant and the second, Paleoophiocordyceps ironomyiae, on the fly.
Some Ophiocordyceps species that prey on ant species today are known as
“zombie-ant fungi”
because the fungal parasite can manipulate the behavior of its hosts for its own benefit. The phenomenon inspired the video game behind the HBO TV show
“The Last of Us.”
HBO shares a parent company, Warner Bros. Discovery, with CNN.
“The discovery of these two fossils suggests that terrestrial ecosystems were already very complex, and that Ophiocordyceps, in particular, may have begun to act as “predators” of insects in the Cretaceous period, regulating the populations of certain groups,” Zhuang said via email.
An ant infected with parasitic fungus trapped in 99 million-year-old amber.
Nanjing Institute of Geology and Palaeontology, Chinese Academy of Sciences/NIGPAS
Zombie fungi then and now
Today, parasitic fungi, also known as entomopathogenic fungi, infect a wide range of insect groups, including ants, flies, spiders, cicadas and beetles, according to London’s Natural History Museum.
In the case of carpenter ants, the spore of the Ophiocordyceps fungus lands on the head of an ant, enters its brain through a weak area in the insect’s exoskeleton and takes control of the ant to facilitate its spread, said Conrad Labandeira, senior scientist and curator of fossil arthropods at the Smithsonian Museum of Natural History in Washington, DC, who wasn’t involved in the study.
Paleoophiocordyceps likely zombified its hosts in similar ways, according to Labandeira.
“It appears that ants, for some reason, were targeted early for zombification, and currently are the major recipients of this parasitoid fungus,” Labandeira said. He added that flies are only rarely affected by these parasitic fungi today, making a fossilized example particularly interesting.
The species of fungus that infected the prehistoric ant may be an ancestor of zombie-ant fungi, and thus likely controlled its host’s body in similar ways, said study coauthor João Araújo, mycology curator and assistant professor at the Danish Natural History Museum. Very few specimens of ancient parasitic fungi have been discovered, so little is known about their evolution.
The two insects were likely killed by the fungi before getting trapped in the sticky tree resin that ultimately forms amber, said Araújo, noting that most entomopathogenic fungi kill their hosts to produce the fruiting body.
This lost parasite diversity had a significant role in shaping the planet we live on today, said Phil Barden, an associate professor at New Jersey Institute of Technology’s department of biological sciences, who has worked on amber fossils.
“Even as we find a remarkable diversity of organisms entombed in amber, it’s important to remember that we really do only capture the smallest glimpse. For any given fossil ant or beetle, we can imagine all of the parasites, fungus, and bacteria that such insects support,” Barden, who wasn’t involved in the new study, said via email.
A spider that has been killed by an entomopathogenic fungus.
Anton Sorokin/Alamy Stock Photo
It was “fascinating to see some of the strangeness of the natural world that we see today was also present at the height of the age of the dinosaurs,” said study coauthor Edmund Jarzembowski, a professor and associate

data.title: Touching the back wall of the Apple store
data.author: nivethan
data.article_summary: 本文讲述了作者高中时和朋友在苹果专卖店玩的一个游戏：试图在不与店员交谈的情况下摸到店后墙并离开。由于店内允许顾客随意触摸展示商品，作者和朋友们常去店里闲逛，但店员总会主动提供帮助。游戏的成功与否全凭运气，人少时较容易，人多时则可能混入人群。作者最终用暑期打工的钱购买了第一台iPod，感受到一种从玩笑到真正消费的转变。作者还回忆起之前的MP3播放器，尽管不记得品牌，但它引发了对媒体盗版和技术探索的兴趣，对作者后来的技术发展影响深远。
data.comments_summary:

44393307.article_content:
Touching the back wall of the Apple store
23 Jun, 2025
Here's a dumb story. When I was in high school, my friends and I had a game we used to play at the mall: we would go into the Apple store and try to make it to the back wall of the store, touch it, and exit out the front without an Apple staff person talking to us.
We were fascinated with the Apple store in the mall because it was essentially an interactive luxury goods store where they'd let you actually
grasp
all the luxury goods with your teenager hands. I have no idea what the current policy is in Apple stores, but in the 2000s, the Apple store in my local mall allowed crowds of greasy teens to wander in and start very obviously just fucking around and poking and prodding everything. They would, however, always try to talk to us and ask us whether they could help us.
So we made up a game where you'd try to get through the store and to the back wall and out again without being spoken to. There were no real strategies here - it was all down to luck and just physically avoiding the Apple store workers. It was not, in my experience, possible to melt into the environment and look like someone who shouldn't be spoken to. Apple store staff would speak to
anyone.
If the store was crowded enough, you could melt into the crowd a bit, but it was no guarantee. The back of the store was always the easiest place to get caught, and touching the back wall was a pretty conspicuous, attention-grabbing action. I think I only won the game a couple times. I had friends who won by sprinting out of the store once or twice.
I bought my first iPod - an iPod 5, I think? - with the salary from my first big summer job. It was more of a stipend than a proper salary, because I was a camp counselor at a summer camp for girls with diabetes, and I was working deranged schedules, and living at my workplace, and my only sustained chunk of free time every day was between 8 PM and midnight, so I was effectively working for 20 hours a day.
They did not pay us a ton for this! But I made enough money from that job to buy an iPod when I returned home for a few weeks before going to my freshman year of college.
Anyway, I remember feeling shocked and kind of disembodied and terrified to have
a reason,
finally, to personally purchase something from the Luxury Goods Store Which Is Also An Interactive Playplace. I remember that I was acting very strangely during the entire process, speaking oddly to the salesperson, kind of terrified to be spending that much money... but I couldn't get myself to lighten up. Part of my brain was saying "this place is bullshit and I use it to clown on the staff," and part of my brain was saying
"I want the luxury good!!
and I am going to purchase it now." Much dissonance. I got the iPod and I loved it, though.
I also remember realizing at this time that the reason the Apple store allowed crowds of greasy teens in to prod everything was that we were one of the
target audiences
for the luxury goods, and it was good for Apple that we were fascinated with their store. They were not asking us if we wanted an iPod because they were trying to interrupt our game - they
really did
think we might want to buy an iPod, because we really might have been actual customers. I was still 18 years old when I bought mine. I did not look any different, really, than I had a few months before, when we were still playing our game in high school.
The MP3 player I had before that iPod was a much more generic one. I've spent the last few days occasionally checking Wikipedia and other places online to see if I can tell which one it was, and I have absolutely no idea. It might have been a Creative? It certainly wasn't a Zune. I think my parents got it at Walmart.
It left a bigger impact on my life, really, than the iPod, because it was the thing that got me into media piracy, and led me to install Linux on an old laptop, which I used exclusively for media piracy. This increased my computer proficiency dramatically (though not to the point where I became a habitual Linux user) and set off a chain of events that made me much more comfortable with amateur web development and eventually game development.
It's a shame I cannot remember what brand it was! I remember the iPod because it was a luxury good, but I think I owe that old Walmart MP3 player a lot more.
#apple

data.title: My home servers are not a homelab
data.author: nradk
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了“家庭实验室”（homelab）的概念，指在家中设置的用于实验和学习的服务器、网络设备等基础设施，规模和形式多样，从单个旧手机到完整的数据中心。作者有自己的服务器 setup，用于自托管服务，但并不称为家庭实验室，因为缺乏实验和学习的目的，仅用于维护和改进。作者纠结于如何准确命名这种 setup，认为“家庭服务器”（home server）并不完全合适，并提出其他可能的名称如“HomeCloud”或“HomeProd”，但未有定论。最终强调命名并非重大问题，但反映出不同用户目的和用途的差异。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于“homelab”这一术语的定义、用途和命名争议

不同观点：
• **反对“homelab”术语，认为其无意义**：
  - [udev4096] 认为“homelab”是无事生非，没有实际意义，并将其与“隐私剧场”类比，暗示这只是为了吸引注意力。
  - [jumploops] 用幽默的方式将“homelab”比作“水坑”，强调其缺乏容错和高可用性，并指出社区中许多人只是为了“教育”目的购买设备，实际上是追求“网络点数”。

  - [ranger207] 强调自己的家庭服务器既是实验室也是生产环境，支持将家庭服务器称为“homelab”。

44418424.article_content:
First, what is a homelab? While I don’t think there’s a dictionary definition, a homelab seems to refer loosely to the collection of servers, networking gear, and supporting infrastructure that someone has set up in their home, for experimentation and learning, either for fun or to develop skills.
Naturally, homelabs can take a wide variety of sizes and shapes. Take a quick look around
/r/homelab
on Reddit, and you’ll find setups ranging from a
single old Android phone
to a
full-fledged data center
. Whatever the scale, the ethos of the subreddit (and other Homelab communities I’ve seen outside of Reddit) seems to be centered around learning, experimentation and playing around. People often have big, expensive and crazy setups just for the heck of it.
At my home, I have a setup that looks like a homelab. It consists of a small rack housing a few computers, a switch, and a few other supporting pieces of hardware. But I don’t consider this a homelab, because I don’t use it as a
lab
. It sits there, running the ten or so services I self-host for me and my family. When I work on it, it is for regular maintainence, incremental improvement, or to install new services. I do enjoy working on it, and I’ve learned a lot along the way, but these are merely side effects.
So I hesitate to call it a homelab, and there’s this small lexical vacuum here—no other word applies well. ‘Home server’ comes close, but it feels strange to refer to the whole setup, consisting of multiple servers and other non-server equipment, in the singular as a ‘home server’. ‘Home servers’ isn’t ideal either. I usually just refer it to as my ‘self-hosting setup’. Yeah, I know I’m splitting hairs—it isn’t that big of a deal what you call things. But I think it is interesting that within the set of people who keep servers in their home, there are two subsets (with considerable overlap) whose reasons for doing so are sort of orthogonal. The ‘homelab’ moniker perfectly fits one group, and it would be nice for the self-hosters whose setups are not homelabs to have a cool name too. ‘HomeCloud’? ‘HomeProd’? Stick to ‘home server(s)’? I don’t have any good ideas.

data.title: WorldVLA: Towards Autoregressive Action World Model
data.author: chrsw
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一种名为WorldVLA的自动回归动作世界模型，该模型整合了视觉-语言-动作（VLA）模型和世界模型。WorldVLA通过结合动作和图像的理解与生成，预测未来图像并学习环境的基本物理规则，从而改进动作生成。同时，动作模型基于图像观察生成后续动作，帮助视觉理解并促进世界模型的视觉生成。研究显示，WorldVLA的表现优于单独的动作和世界模型，展现了二者之间的相互增强效果。然而，动作模型在以自动回归方式生成动作序列时性能下降，原因是模型对动作预测的泛化能力有限，导致早期动作误差影响后续动作。为此，文章提出了一种注意力掩码策略，通过选择性掩码先前动作来显著提升动作块生成的性能。

不同观点：

- **论据**：blovescoffee指出，**autoregressive action world model**虽然目前表现良好，但可能只是阶段性的最佳方案（local max），未来JEPA等新方法可能会提供更大的突破。
- **隐含的讨论**：对AI模型的架构选择和未来发展方向存在不同预期，部分人可能更看好新方法（如JEPA）的潜力。

View a PDF of the paper titled WorldVLA: Towards Autoregressive Action World Model, by Jun Cen and 11 other authors
View PDF
HTML (experimental)
Abstract:
We present WorldVLA, an autoregressive action world model that unifies action and image understanding and generation. Our WorldVLA intergrates Vision-Language-Action (VLA) model and world model in one single framework. The world model predicts future images by leveraging both action and image understanding, with the purpose of learning the underlying physics of the environment to improve action generation. Meanwhile, the action model generates the subsequent actions based on image observations, aiding in visual understanding and in turn helps visual generation of the world model. We demonstrate that WorldVLA outperforms standalone action and world models, highlighting the mutual enhancement between the world model and the action model. In addition, we find that the performance of the action model deteriorates when generating sequences of actions in an autoregressive manner. This phenomenon can be attributed to the model's limited generalization capability for action prediction, leading to the propagation of errors from earlier actions to subsequent ones. To address this issue, we propose an attention mask strategy that selectively masks prior actions during the generation of the current action, which shows significant performance improvement in the action chunk generation task.

data.title: The Chan-Zuckerbergs stopped funding social causes
data.author: 1vuio0pswjnm7
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：慈善资金与社会责任在教育领域的角色与影响

不同观点：
• **ggm** 认为，国家需求的资金应通过税收来提供，而不是依赖慈善资金。如果依赖慈善资金，应将其放入一个安全的机制中，以防止不确定的结果。
• **maxglute** 对慈善资金未用于建设博物馆等实体设施表示不满，认为这是缺乏对社会责任的体现。
• **asveikau** 从家长角度出发，强调学校突然关闭对家庭造成的混乱和影响，认为亿万富翁在有能力的情况下，不继续资助学校是道德上的耻辱。
• **duxup** 对学校使用高科技设备如“语音计步器”表示质疑，认为这些技术并不能解决教育的根本问题，尤其是在缺乏纪律规定的情况下。
• **southernplaces7** 提出两种可能性：要么是 cynical liars 为了公关价值资助社会项目，现在不再关心；要么是懦夫，不能坚持他们声称道德上支持的事业。不论是哪种情况，最终受害者都是依赖这些项目的人们。
• **ars** 认为如果Chan的实验没有效果，那么不再资助是合理的，尤其是因为教育周期不可能等待20年。
• **Jedd** 引用了《No Such Thing As a Free Gift: The Gates Foundation and the Price of Philanthropy》一书，暗示对慈善资本主义的质疑。
• **max_** 提到Chan和Zuckerberg之前在Newark公共学校的资助项目也遭到质疑，认为资金被浪费了。
• **apical_dendrite** 认为Chan和Zuckerberg在处理资助退出时比Elon和Trump更负责任，后者更 abruptly 地打破了承诺。
• **itsthecourier** 分享个人经验，强调即使尽力资助他人，也应理解其中的不确定性。
• **MilnerRoute** 引用了《华盛顿邮报》的标题，强调了Chan和Zuckerberg停止资助对社会造成的直接影响。
• **jongjong** 认为亿万富翁不应介入社会事业，最好去购买游艇和豪宅，以免资助可能有害的项目，并认为让亿万富翁感觉自己赢得了人生游戏，可以减少其参与有害政治的倾向。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于亿万富翁是否应该以及如何承担社会责任，特别是在教育领域。
• 一些评论质疑高科技在教育中的实际效果和适用性。
• 另一个值得注意的点是慈善资金的可持续性和不确定性，以及对依赖这些资金的社区的潜在影响。
• 不同评论者对亿万富翁在社会项目中的角色持有截然不同的看法，有人认为他们应更负责任，有人则希望他们完全退出社会事业。

data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：网站界面变化及其在不同设备上的表现

不同观点：
• [tomhow] 确认已经知晓问题，并表示相关人员会在有空时处理，暗示问题尚未解决。
• [Averave] 通过对比网页代码的变化，指出HTML结构的改变导致了显示问题。具体变化是从使用 `<tr>` 增加空间改为 `<td style="height:10px">`，并且新方法在桌面端有效，但在移动端无效。该用户还提出了一种通过开发者工具手动修复问题的方法。
• [masklinn] 提到在手机上的一些具体变化，如主链接从两行变成三行，以及个人资料和退出登录按钮从两行变成一行。虽然这些变化使得某些操作（如点击新帖子）更麻烦，但也减少了误触退出登录的可能性。
• [ajjenkins] 确认问题存在，特别是在iOS Safari浏览器上，文章标题距离顶部过近。
• [leakycap] 对网站的小改动表示兴趣，并表示欣赏网站多年来保持一致的外观，尽管这些小变化可能并不总是受欢迎。
• [josephcsible] 和 [LordShredda] 都表示自己也注意到了这个问题，后者甚至一度以为是自己的Firefox Beta版本导致了布局错误。
• [RandomBacon] 特别指出在Firefox for Android上也观察到了这个问题。
• [kurrupttt] 持不同意见，表示自己测试时没有发现任何问题，暗示问题可能与具体设备或浏览器有关。

补充讨论：
• 争议的焦点在于HTML结构的改变是否合适，尤其是新方法在移动端的表现不佳，导致用户体验受到影响。
• 部分用户对网站的微小变化持批评态度，认为这些变化破坏了原有的用户体验，而另一些用户则对这些小改动持开放或中立态度。

data.title: Use keyword-only arguments in Python dataclasses
data.author: Bogdanp
data.article_summary:
Python的**dataclasses**是一个方便构造数据类的好功能，可以替代字典，并支持添加方法、动态属性和子类。相比手写类，dataclasses自动生成`__init__()`和`__eq__()`等方法，简化了开发。为了提高可维护性，建议使用`kw_only=True`参数，强制使用关键字参数调用，如`MyDataClass(x=1, y='foo', z=False)`。这样有两个好处：  
1. 允许重新排序字段而不破坏调用者。  
2. 允许子类添加必需字段，不受默认值限制。  
对于需要保证向后兼容性和可扩展性的库作者尤其重要。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Python中关键字仅限参数（keyword-only arguments）的使用及其优缺点

不同观点：
• **支持使用关键字仅限参数**：
   - **meander_water** 介绍了如何通过 `KW_ONLY` 实现关键字仅限参数，认为这是明确函数参数的一种好方法。
   - **joshdavham** 提到这种方法可以避免因参数顺序改变而导致的调用代码出错问题，认为有助于防止未来的不兼容变更。

• **反对或对关键字仅限参数持保留态度**：
   - **FridgeSeal** 提到 Boto3 库的大量使用 `**kwargs` 导致参数不明确，认为这种方式让开发者依赖文档和IDE提示，体验较差。
   - **ayhanfuat** 认为关键字仅限参数在变量名已经匹配的情况下变得冗长，期望Python能有JavaScript那样的简写语法。

• **对数据类的限制表示不满**：
   - **est** 提到Python的数据类无法存储额外的键值对，无法直接将字典传递给数据类，必须使用支持的键，这限制了灵活性。

• **讨论更广泛的应用场景**：
   - **flakes** 认为强制使用关键字参数在参数数量超过4-5个或参数相似度较高时能提高可读性，但对于少量且明确的参数，这样做会增加不必要的冗长。

补充讨论：
• **joshdavham** 指出，虽然关键字仅限参数能防止未来变更带来的问题，但在现有项目中引入这种变更也可能导致兼容性问题。

44418036.article_content:
Python
dataclasses
are a really nice feature for constructing classes that primarily hold or work with data. They can be a good alternative to using dictionaries, since they allow you to add methods, dynamic properties, and subclasses. They can also be a good alternative to building your own class by hand, since they don’t need a custom
__init__()
that reassigns attributes and provide methods like
__eq__()
out of the box.
One small tip to keeping dataclasses maintainable is to always construct them with
kw_only=True
, like so:
from dataclasses import dataclass
@dataclass(kw_only=True)
class MyDataClass:
x: int
y: str
z: bool = True
This will construct an
__init__()
that looks like this:
class MyDataClass:
def __init__(
self,
*,
x: int,
y: str,
z: bool = True,
) -> None:
self.x = x
self.y = y
self.z = z
Instead of:
class MyDataClass:
def __init__(
self,
x: int,
y: str,
z: bool = True,
) -> None:
self.x = x
self.y = y
self.z = z
That
*
in the argument list means everything that follows must be passed as a keyword argument, instead of a positional argument.
There are two reasons you probably want to do this:
It allows you to reorder the fields on the dataclass without breaking callers. Positional arguments means a caller can use
MyDataClass(1, 'foo', False)
, and if you remove/reorder any of these arguments, you’ll break those callers unexpectedly. By forcing callers to use
MyDataClass(x=1, y='foo', z=False)
, you remove this risk.
It allows subclasses to add required fields. Normally, any field with a default value (like
z
above) will force any fields following it to also have a default. And that includes
all
fields defined by subclasses. Using
kw_only=True
gives subclasses the flexibility to decide for themselves which fields must be provided by the caller and which have a default.
These reasons are more important for library authors than anything. We spend a lot of time trying to ensure backwards-compatibility and forwards-extensibility in
Review Board
, so this is an important topic for us. And if you’re developing something reusable with dataclasses, it might be for you, too.

data.title: Inline-C: Write inline C in Haskell
data.author: burnt-resistor
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了Haskell库`inline-c`，它允许开发者直接在Haskell代码中嵌入C语言代码。这个库简化了Haskell与C的互操作，使得调用C函数和使用C数据结构变得更加方便。通过`inline-c`，开发者可以在Haskell源码中编写C代码片段，并自动处理两者之间的数据转换和内存管理。该库支持GHC编译器，并且适用于需要高性能或与C语言库交互的项目。注意事项包括确保C代码的正确性和处理潜在的跨语言内存管理问题。

data.title: ICE test train reaches speeds of up to 405.0 km/h
data.author: doener
data.article_summary: 2025年6月28日，德铁（DB）与西门子交通在埃尔福特—莱比锡/哈勒高速线路的测试中，使用ICE试验列车达到了405公里/小时的速度。此类高速测试极为罕见，仅用于检测目的。德铁InfraGO总裁Nagl博士强调，这一成就证明了该线路基础设施的卓越性能，经过10年运营仍能支持高速运行。联邦交通部国务秘书Hirte指出，该测试彰显了德国高品质基础设施和强大工业能力。西门子交通的Velaro Novo试验列车在测试中表现优异，其新一代技术显著提升了能效和运力，并降低了成本。德铁Systemtechnik的ICE-S试验列车配备先进测量技术，用于检测和优化高速线路。Velaro Novo列车经过多年测试，展现了其灵活适应未来需求的能力。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：德国高速列车（ICE）在埃尔福特-莱比锡/哈勒线路上的测试及其意义

不同观点：
• **chmod775**：认为文章表达不清，实际上的突破不在于列车本身能达到多高速度，因为很多ICE列车已经有能力达到类似速度。真正的挑战在于普通线路（非测试线路）能支持如此高速运行，建设并维护高速且安全、经济适用的轨道才是关键。
• **doener**：引用新闻，强调此次测试的意义在于展示现有基础设施能够支持高速列车运行，且测试提供了关于列车声学、空气动力学等方面的重要数据，有助于未来高速列车的研发。
• **fjfaase**：对德国列车系统的现状表示不满，认为尽管此次测试展示了技术成就，但德国列车准点率和维护问题严重，公众可能不会为此感到兴奋。
• **tootyskooty**：指出ICE列车速度已经足够快，问题在于它们与慢速列车共用轨道，导致延误无法通过提速弥补，投资慢速列车的性价比可能更高。
• **floydian10**：抱怨列车准点率低及重要路线关闭时间过长，认为这些基础问题未解决前，速度提升意义有限。
• **KingOfCoders**：引用Amdahl's law，暗示德国列车速度限制是综合因素的结果，大多数列车最高时速限制在250-300km/h是合理的。
• **sMarsIntruder**：提到2000年代初在意大利的测试已经超过500km/h，质疑此次测试的创新性。
• **snambi**：同样质疑此次测试的特殊性，指出已有其他列车能达到更高速度。

补充讨论：
• **WorkerBee28474**：澄清“ICE”指的是城际快车，而非内燃机车，避免误解。
• **WastedCucumber** 和 **Kunsang**：以幽默方式调侃列车可能延误或使用过时技术，虽未提供实质性论据，但反映了部分公众对列车系统的不满情绪。
• **brian-armstrong**：简单提到测试运行，未展开具体观点。

争议焦点：
• 此次测试是否具有实际意义和创新性，一部分人认为轨道支持高速运行是关键突破，另一部分人则质疑列车速度本身没有新意。
• 对德国列车系统的整体满意度，部分评论抱怨准点率和维护问题，认为这些基础问题未解决前，速度提升的实际意义有限。

28. Juni 2025, 17:00 Uhr
Erfurt
Die Deutsche Bahn (DB) und Siemens Mobility haben mit einem ICE-Testzug auf der Schnellfahrstrecke Erfurt–Leipzig/Halle eine Geschwindigkeit von 405,0
km/h erreicht. Fahrten mit Geschwindigkeiten über 300 km/h sind sehr selten auf dem deutschen Schienennetz und werden nur zu Testzwecken durchgeführt.
Dr. Philipp Nagl, Vorstandsvorsitzender der DB InfraGO AG:
„Heute ist ein ICE so schnell wie noch nie über die Strecke Erfurt–Leipzig/Halle gefahren. 405,0 km/h als neuer Höchstwert sind auch eine Bestätigung für die Leistungsfähigkeit der Infrastruktur auf dieser Schnellfahrstrecke: Nach 10 Jahren in Dauerbetrieb können wir problemlos und ohne Anpassungen mit so hohen Geschwindigkeiten fahren. Es ist eine Bestätigung dafür, dass Infrastrukturinvestitionen über Generationen hinweg die Grundlage für zuverlässige, nachhaltige und leistungsfähige Mobilität und Logistik sind. Die Testfahrten liefern uns wichtige Erkenntnisse für die Sanierung und Instandhaltung von Schnellfahrstrecken sowie die technische Weiterentwicklung von Hochgeschwindigkeitszügen und kommen somit auch den Fahrgästen zugute.“
Christian Hirte, Parlamentarischer Staatssekretär beim Bundesminister für Verkehr
: „Deutschland ist und kann Spitze! Die heutige Höchstgeschwindigkeitsfahrt belegt, dass wir in Deutschland über eine hochwertige Infrastruktur und leistungsfähige Industrie verfügen. Die dabei gewonnenen Testergebnisse werden für die DB AG bei künftigen Beschaffungen und für die Kunden von hohem Nutzen sein, so dass sie schnell, sicher und pünktlich ihr Ziel erreichen. Diese Hochgeschwindigkeitsfahrt stärkt außerdem die Stellung Deutschlands als Wirtschafts- und Exportnation.“
Thomas Graetz, Vice President High Speed and Intercity Trains, Siemens Mobility
: „Die erfolgreichen Testfahrten unseres Velaro Novo Testwagens, der heute eine Geschwindigkeit von 405,0
km/h erreichte, zeigen eindrucksvoll die Leistungsfähigkeit unserer neuesten Generation von Hochgeschwindigkeitszügen. Unser Ziel war es, tiefgehende Erkenntnisse in Akustik, Aerodynamik und Fahrverhalten bei extremen Geschwindigkeiten zu sammeln – dieses Ziel haben wir heute dank der exzellenten Zusammenarbeit mit der DB InfraGO AG und DB Systemtechnik erreicht. Der Velaro Novo wird die Schienenverkehrstechnik revolutionieren, indem er neue Standards für Kapazität, Wirtschaftlichkeit und Effizienz setzt. Solche Innovationen sind der Schlüssel zu einer nachhaltigen und zukunftsorientierten Mobilität.“
Dr. Hiie-Mai Unger, Vorsitzende der Geschäftsführung der DB Systemtechnik
: „Innovationen voranbringen und den Zugverkehr erfolgreich für die Zukunft aufstellen – dafür leisten wir als DB Systemtechnik mit unseren Testfahrten einen wichtigen Beitrag. Mit unserem Hochgeschwindigkeitsmesszug ,ICE-S‘ konnten wir heute viele wichtige Informationen unter anderem zu Akustik, Aerodynamik, Fahrverhalten und dem Zusammenspiel von Zug und Schiene bei sehr hohen Geschwindigkeiten sammeln. Diese Erkenntnisse helfen uns bei weiteren Streckensanierungen und dabei, den Bahnbetrieb und speziell den Hochgeschwindigkeitsverkehr weiter zu optimieren.“
Bezeugen den Geschwindigkeitsrekord (von links): Thomas Graetz, Vice President High Speed and Intercity Trains, Siemens Mobility, Dr. Philipp Nagl, Vorstandsvorsitzender der DB InfraGO AG, Christian Hirte, Parlamentarischer Staatssekretär beim Bundesminister für Verkehr, Diana Herbstreuth, Mitglied des Deutschen Bundestages, und Dr. Hiie-Mai Unger, Vorsitzende der Geschäftsführung der DB Systemtechnik. (Copyright: DB AG/Patrick Kuschfeld)
Der ICE-S der DB Systemtechnik wird hauptsächlich für Test- und Messfahrten eingesetzt. Er dient dazu, neue Strecken zu testen, die Infrastruktur zu untersuchen und verschiedene Hochgeschwindigkeitsprüfungen durchzuführen. Um die Fahrtbedingungen auf den Hochgeschwindigkeitsstrecken präzise zu analysieren und zu optimieren, ist er mit umfangreicher Messtechnik ausgestattet. Damit spielt der ICE-S eine essenzielle Rolle bei der Weiterentwicklung und Sicherstellung der Leistungsfähigkeit des deutschen Hochgeschwindigkeitsnetzes.
Der neue Velaro Novo von Siemens Mobility ist eine konsequente Weiterentwicklung von drei Velaro-Generationen. Zahlreiche Innovationen im Detail machen den neuen Hochgeschwindigkeitszug zu einem hocheffizienten Fahrzeug, das bis zu 30 Prozent weniger Energie verbraucht und die Investitions- und Instandhaltungskosten deutlich reduziert. Gleichzeitig wurde die Sitzplatzkapazität um zehn Prozent erhöht. Der Velaro Novo ist durch zahlreiche Konfigurationsmöglichkeiten zukunftssicher und lässt sich auch noch nach Jahren im Betrieb an neue Vorstellungen und Anforderungen der Betreiber flexibel anpassen. Der Velaro Novo Testwagen mit dem Namen #seeitnovo wird seit mehreren Jahren auf dem deutschen Fernverkehrsnetz erprobt.

• **snambi**：同样质疑此次测试的特殊性，指出已有其他列车能达到更高速度。

补充讨论：
• **WorkerBee28474**：澄清“ICE”指的是城际快车，而非内燃机车，避免误解。
• **WastedCucumber** 和 **Kunsang**：以幽默方式调侃列车可能延误或使用过时技术，虽未提供实质性论据，但反映了部分公众对列车系统的不满情绪。
• **brian-armstrong**：简单提到测试运行，未展开具体观点。

争议焦点：
• 此次测试是否具有实际意义和创新性，一部分人认为轨道支持高速运行是关键突破，另一部分人则质疑列车速度本身没有新意。
• 对德国列车系统的整体满意度，部分评论抱怨准点率和维护问题，认为这些基础问题未解决前，速度提升的实际意义有限。

Using DuckDB WASM + Cloudflare R2 to host and query big data (for almost free)
The motivation here, prompted by a recent question
Abigail Haddad
had on LinkedIn:
For the machines, the context is hosting a dataset of 150 million rows (in another post Abigail stated it was around 72 gigs). And you want the public to be able to make ad-hoc queries on that data. Examples where you may want to do this are public dashboards (think a cities open data site, just puts all the data on R2 and has a front end).
This is the point where traditional SQL databases for websites probably don’t make sense. Databases like
Supabase Postgres
or MySQL can have that much data, given the cost of cloud computing though and what they are typically used for, it does not make much sense to put 72 gigs and use them for data analysis type queries.
Hosting the data as static files though in an online bucket, like
Cloudflare’s R2
, and then querying the data makes more sense for that size. Here to query the data, I also use a
WASM deployed DuckDB
. What this means is I don’t really have to worry about a server at all – it should scale to however many people want to use the service (I am just serving up HTML). The client’s machine handles creating the query and displaying the resulting data via javascript, and Cloudflare basically just pushes data around.
If you want to see it in action, you can check out the
github repo
, or see the
demo deployed on github pages
to illustrate generating queries. To check out a query on my Cloudflare R2 bucket, you can run
SELECT * FROM 'https://data-crimedecoder.com/books.parquet' LIMIT 10;
:
Cloudflare is nice here, since there are no egress charges (big data you need to worry about that). You do get charged for different read/write operations, but the free tiers seem quite generous (I do not know quite how to map these queries to Class B operations in Cloudflare’s parlance, but you get 10 million per month and all my tests only generated a few thousand).
For some notes on this set-up. On Cloudflare, to be able to use DuckDB WASM, I needed to expose the R2 bucket via a custom domain. Using the development url did not work (same
issue as here
). I also set my CORS Policy to:
[
{
"AllowedOrigins": [
"*"
],
"AllowedMethods": [
"GET",
"HEAD"
],
"AllowedHeaders": [
"*"
],
"ExposeHeaders": [],
"MaxAgeSeconds": 3000
}
]
While my Crime De-Coder site is PHP, all the good stuff happens client-side. So you can see some example demo’s of the
GSU book prices data
.
One of the annoying things about this though, with S3 you can partition the files and
query multiple partitions at once
. Here something like
SELECT * FROM read_parquet('https://data-crimedecoder.com/parquet/Semester=*/*') LIMIT 10;
does not work. You can union the partitions together manually. So not sure if there is a way to set up R2 to work the same way as the S3 example (set up a FTP server? let me know in the comments!).
For pricing, for the scenario Abigail had of 72 gigs of data, we then have:
$10 per year for the domain
0.015*72*12 = $13
for storage of the 72 gigs
So we have a total cost to run this of $23 per year. And it can scale to a crazy number of users and very large datasets out of the box. (My usecase here is just $10 for the domain, you get 10 gigs for free.)
Since this can be deployed on a static site, there are free options (like github pages). So the page with the SQL query part is essentially free. (I am not sure if there is a way to double dip on the R2 custom domain, such as just putting the HTML in the bucket.)
While this example only shows generating a table, you can do whatever additional graphics client side. So could make a normal looking dashboard with dropdowns, and those just execute various queries and fill in the graphs/tables.

data.title: Oldest boomerang doesn't come back
data.author: ljf
data.article_summary: 考古学家发现，世界上已知最古老的回力镖有约40,000年历史，比此前认为的更古老。这把由猛犸象牙精心制作的回力镖于1985年在波兰的Oblazowa洞穴出土，不会回飞，可能用于狩猎或仪式。这一发现展示了早期智人的高超工艺和行为复杂性。尽管回力镖常与澳大利亚土著文化相关，但在欧洲等地也有发现，表明这种工具曾在不同大陆使用。该研究发表于《PLOS One》期刊。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：古人类使用的工具，特别是回力棒（或投掷棒）的用途和功能

不同观点：
• [paleotrope] 认为这种工具展示了人类行为的高超洞察力，尤其是早期智人能够制作出适合手握并用于狩猎的完美物体。他指出，这类工具虽然不是非常复杂，但比普通石头更符合手感和用途。此外，他强调大多数投掷棒（包括回力棒）并不会返回给投掷者，因为那在狩猎中并不实用。

• [yabatopia] 同意该工具可能用于狩猎，但提出它也可能具有文化和艺术价值，甚至可能用于某种仪式。他对学术界常使用“仪式”作为解释表示质疑，认为有时直接承认“我们不知道”反而更诚实。

• [delichon] 持不同意见，坚持认为回力棒的定义就是会返回给投掷者的工具，因此不能返回的投掷棒不能被称为回力棒，只是普通的投掷 sticks。

• [accoil] 对回力棒是否需要“返回”功能提出疑问，质疑返回功能在实际使用中的价值。

• [B1FF_PSUVM] 调侃地表示，这种不会返回的工具只是比“大棍子”稍微高级一点，暗示其功能性并没有那么特别。

补充讨论：
• 回力棒是否必须具备返回功能是争议的焦点，delichon 强调定义问题，而 accoil 和 paleotrope 则质疑返回功能在实际应用中的必要性。
• yabatopia 对工具用途的多元解释提出质疑，认为学术解释有时过于依赖仪式等模糊概念，而不是承认未知。

Image source,
Maciej Biernacki
Image caption,
The boomerang was found near stones, animal and human bones
Helen Briggs
BBC environment correspondent
@hbriggs
Published
26 June 2025
The world's oldest boomerang is older than previously thought, casting new light on the ingenuity of humans living at the time.
The tool, which was found in a cave in Poland in 1985, is now thought to be 40,000 years old.
Archaeologists say it was fashioned from a mammoth's tusk with an astonishing level of skill.
Researchers worked out from its shape that it would have flown when thrown, but would not have come back to the thrower.
It was probably used in hunting, though it might have had cultural or artistic value, perhaps being used in some kind of ritual.
Image source,
Talamo et al., 2025, PLOS One, CC-BY 4.0
Image caption,
The ivory boomerang is curved and about the size of a baseball bat
The mammoth ivory boomerang was unearthed in Oblazowa Cave in southern Poland.
It was originally thought to be about 30,000 years old. But new, more reliable radiocarbon dating of human and animal bones found at the site puts the age at between 39,000 and 42,000 years old.
"It's the oldest boomerang in the world, and the only one in the world made of this shape and this long to be found in Poland," said Dr Sahra Talamo of the University of Bologna, Italy.
It gives a "remarkable insight" into human behaviour, she said, particularly how Homo sapiens living as long as 42,000 years ago could shape "such a perfect object" with the knowledge it could be used to hunt animals.
The boomerang is exceptionally well preserved, with score marks suggesting it had been polished and carved for use by a right-handed individual.
Image source,
Talamo et al., 2025, PLOS One, CC-BY 4.0
Image caption,
The entrance to Oblazowa Cave on the southern border of Poland
Boomerangs are generally associated with Aboriginal culture in Australia.
However, rare finds in the historical record outside Australia suggest they were used across different continents.
The oldest known boomerang from Australia dates to about 10,500 years ago, made from wood. But the oldest images of boomerangs in Australia are rock art paintings 20,000 years old, according to National Museum Australia.
A wooden boomerang dating back 7,000 years has been found in Jutland, a peninsula between Denmark and Germany, while fragments of a 2,000-year-old oak boomerang â which does come back â has been found in The Netherlands.
The research by a team of scientists from Poland, Italy, Germany, France, Switzerland and the UK is published in the journal
PLOS One.

AI SDK CPP
The AI SDK CPP is a modern C++ toolkit designed to help you build AI-powered applications with popular model providers like OpenAI and Anthropic. It provides a unified, easy-to-use API that abstracts away the complexity of different provider implementations.
Motivation
C++ developers have long lacked a first-class, convenient way to interact with modern AI services like OpenAI, Anthropic, and others. AI SDK CPP bridges this gap by providing:
Unified API
: Work with multiple AI providers through a single, consistent interface
Modern C++
: Built with C++20 features for clean, expressive code
Minimal Dependencies
: Minimal external dependencies for easy integration
Installation
You will need a C++20 compatible compiler and CMake 3.16+ installed on your development machine.

data.author: ednite
data.article_summary: 挪威国有博彩公司Norsk Tipping因系统错误，错误地将欧元奖金转换为挪威克朗时放大了100倍，导致数千名彩票中奖者收到高达数百万的错误中奖通知。公司随后更正了奖金数额，并表示没有进行错误的支付。这一失误引发广泛不满，公司CEO Tonje Sagstuen为此道歉并辞职。文化和平等部长Lubna Jaffery表示，这样的错误本不应发生，并要求公司加强控制流程。Norsk Tipping承认近几个月出现多次严重错误和技术问题，并受到监管机构和客户的批评。

44418006.article_content:
Thousands in Norway told they won up to millions in lottery error
13 hours ago
Share
Save
Danai Nesta Kupemba
BBC News
Share
Save
NurPhoto via Getty Images
Eurojackpot tickets are sold across a number of European countries (file photo from Poland)
Scores of Norwegians thought they had become millionaires after receiving a notification from the state-owned gambling company saying they had won eye-watering sums - until it turned out it was a mistake.
"Several thousand" people who won prizes in the Eurojackpot were notified of incorrect amounts on Friday, Norsk Tipping said. The company declined to confirm the exact number of those impacted to the BBC.
Norsk Tipping CEO Tonje Sagstuen apologised and resigned a day later.
An error in the conversion from Eurocents to Norwegian kroner caused the prize amounts to be "excessively high", the company said. The amount was multiplied by 100, instead of being divided by 100, local media reported.
Norsk Tipping receives the prize amounts from Germany in euros, and then converts them to Norwegian kroner.
The correct amounts were updated on Saturday evening. No incorrect pay-outs were made, the gambling company said.
"I am terribly sorry that we have disappointed so many, and I understand that people are angry with us," Ms Sagstuen said in a statement, adding that "criticism is justified" given the "breach of trust".
She said she had received several messages from people who were planning to go on holiday, renovate their homes or buy an apartment.
"To them I can only say: Sorry! But I understand that it is a small consolation," she said.
One woman, in the middle of a renovation project, told Norwegian Broadcasting Corporation (NRK) she received a notification that she had won 1.2 million kroner ($119,000: £87,000), but instead received only a fraction of that sum.
The Norsk Tipping board met with the Ministry of Culture, which administers the running of the company, for an emergency meeting on Saturday.
After the meeting, Ms Sagstuen stepped down from her role as CEO. She held the position since September 2023 and had worked at Norsk Tipping since 2014.
"Here, things have failed in several places, this is my responsibility," she said.
She said she was "sad" to leave but confident in the "improvement processes" that have been put in place.
Minister of Culture and Equality Lubna Jaffery told NRK that "such mistakes should not happen", especially as Norsk Tipping has the exclusive right to deliver gaming services in the country.
"We expect the board to work actively to improve the control routines," she said.
This is not the first time Norsk Tipping has found itself under criticism.
The company said that "several serious errors have been uncovered" in recent months and it had "experienced a number of technical problems in the past year".
It acknowledged it had been "heavily criticised" by the regulator and its customers, and the criticism "was justified".

Orange Pi Nova Teased with Loongson 2K3000 as Loongson Expands Product Line
Jun 29, 2025 — by Giorgio Mendoza

This week, Orange Pi previewed its upcoming Orange Pi Nova, a single-board computer developed in collaboration with Loongson. Announced through Orange Pi’s official channels, the Nova combines the Loongson 2K3000 processor with a range of I/O options and support for up to 32GB of DDR4 RAM.
The
board
uses the Loongson 2K3000 processor, which is designed for industrial control and terminal devices such as notebooks and cloud terminals. This processor is built on Loongson’s own LoongArch instruction set and integrates eight LA364E cores running at up to 2.5 GHz.
— ADVERTISEMENT —
It includes a second-generation GPGPU core (LG200) for graphics and AI tasks, hardware security modules for encryption and trusted computing, and supports video output up to 4K at 60 frames per second.
Orange Pi Nova Bottom View
(click image to enlarge)
Features shown in the teaser include dual network ports with 2.5-gigabit Ethernet and 1-gigabit RJ45 connectors, multiple USB 2.0 ports, one USB 3.0 port, and a USB Type-C port that can also provide power. Display and expansion options include an HDMI output, LCD and eDP connectors.
Orange Pi Nova Top View
(click image to enlarge)
Additional interfaces include UART headers, a 40-pin GPIO header, an RTC connector, MicroSD slot, audio output, PMBus connector, two six-pin CAN headers, a JTAG connector, a debug port, a fan connector, and a slot for Wi-Fi and Bluetooth modules. An SSD NVMe slot is located on the underside of the board, and power can be supplied through a 12-volt DC connector or the adjacent USB Type-C port.
Further Information
The
2025 Loongson Product Release and User Conference
, held at the Zhongguancun International Innovation Center, also introduced Loongson’s new 3C6000 server CPUs and detailed its ongoing work to expand processor performance across desktop, server, industrial control, and AI applications. Loongson highlighted its strategy to maintain control of its own instruction set through the LoongArch architecture and to reduce reliance on foreign technology.
Companies at the event showcased a range of hardware based on Loongson chips, covering use cases such as servers, storage systems, industrial controllers, and security devices. Loongson’s roadmap includes further development of general-purpose CPUs, graphics processors, and AI-focused components, supported by an expanding Linux-based ecosystem.

data.title: Is being bilingual good for your brain?
data.author: Anon84
data.article_summary: 文章讨论了双语能力对大脑的潜在益处。多项研究表明，双语能力可以提高执行功能，如专注力、任务规划和信息更新，甚至可能延缓痴呆症的发生约四年。然而，部分研究结果难以复制，令专家质疑这些益处的真实性及具体表现。总体而言，学习多种语言虽有明显实用优势，但其对认知能力的增强效果仍需进一步研究确认。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：多语言学习的影响与价值

不同观点：
• **多语言学习的认知与文化价值**：
  - [afiodorov] 认为多语言使用让日常生活成为一种脑力锻炼，并强调文化沉浸的重要性。他提到即使长时间使用外语，仍可能无法达到母语般的流利程度。
  - [heresie-dabord] 强调多语言能力不仅有助于沟通，还能打开不同文化和视角的大门，是一种实用的工具，可以有效处理各种问题。
  - [keiferski] 进一步指出，多语言不仅仅是词汇的集合，而是世界观的体现，能让人更具洞察力与理解力。

• **多语言学习的成本与收益**：
  - [hiAndrewQuinn] 认为学习外语的成本高且收益不明显，特别是在成年人的成本效益分析下，除非有强烈的内在动机，否则可能不值得投入。
  - [dehrmann] 提出在时间有限的情况下，是否应选择其他更有效的脑力刺激活动，如演奏乐器或进行身体锻炼。

• **多语言对不同年龄的影响**：
  - [hombre_fatal] 提到不同年龄段的人学习语言对大脑的影响不同，儿童早期的双语优势在后期可能会被单语同龄人追赶上。

• **社会与经济因素的影响**：
  - [dumroll] 认为在像美国这样的国家，多语言可能会带来更多不利因素，如口音问题和社会认同感，且在职业与生活机会上，单语英语者通常表现更好。
  - [Pearledlang] 引用了芬兰瑞典族的例子，指出尽管双语且更富裕，但他们在智商上略低。

• **多语言带来的文化与情感体验**：
  - [FlyingSnake] 强调多语言生活的美妙，能够体验多种语言文化是人类的独特之处，并认为人类天生适合多语言。
  - [qoez] 认为双语言带来的好处更多来自于文化接触，而非单纯的语言能力。

• **语言学习对大脑的独特作用**：
  - [lvl155] 提出早期双语暴露和语言学习时间点对大脑的认知中心形成有影响，晚期的暴露可能仅是增加了翻译能力。
  - [agumonkey] 分享个人经验，认为学习拉丁语等古典语言能重新连接大脑中的概念，带来新的理解。

补充讨论：
- [xvilka] 提到了Language Transfer项目，作为一个学习多语言的资源。
- [qprofyeh] 用技术比喻描述了多语言者在词汇查询和思维转换中的独特体验。

争议焦点：
- 多语言学习是否在实际生活和职业发展中带来显著优势，特别是在以英语为主的国家和环境中，多语言能力是否会带来不利影响。

Is being bilingual good for your brain?
Perhaps. Learning languages offers other, more concrete benefits

Jun 27th 2025

R
eams of papers
have been published on the cognitive advantages of multilingualism. Beyond the conversational doors it can open, multilingualism is supposed to improve “executive function”, a loose concept that includes the ability to ignore distractions, plan complex tasks and update beliefs as new information arrives. Most striking, numerous studies have even shown that bilinguals undergo a later onset of dementia, perhaps of around four years, on average. But some of these studies have failed to replicate, leaving experts wondering whether the effect is real, and if so, what exactly it consists of.

• **多语言学习的成本与收益**：
  - [hiAndrewQuinn] 认为学习外语的成本高且收益不明显，特别是在成年人的成本效益分析下，除非有强烈的内在动机，否则可能不值得投入。
  - [dehrmann] 提出在时间有限的情况下，是否应选择其他更有效的脑力刺激活动，如演奏乐器或进行身体锻炼。

• **多语言对不同年龄的影响**：
  - [hombre_fatal] 提到不同年龄段的人学习语言对大脑的影响不同，儿童早期的双语优势在后期可能会被单语同龄人追赶上。

• **社会与经济因素的影响**：
  - [dumroll] 认为在像美国这样的国家，多语言可能会带来更多不利因素，如口音问题和社会认同感，且在职业与生活机会上，单语英语者通常表现更好。
  - [Pearledlang] 引用了芬兰瑞典族的例子，指出尽管双语且更富裕，但他们在智商上略低。

• **多语言带来的文化与情感体验**：
  - [FlyingSnake] 强调多语言生活的美妙，能够体验多种语言文化是人类的独特之处，并认为人类天生适合多语言。
  - [qoez] 认为双语言带来的好处更多来自于文化接触，而非单纯的语言能力。

• **语言学习对大脑的独特作用**：
  - [lvl155] 提出早期双语暴露和语言学习时间点对大脑的认知中心形成有影响，晚期的暴露可能仅是增加了翻译能力。
  - [agumonkey] 分享个人经验，认为学习拉丁语等古典语言能重新连接大脑中的概念，带来新的理解。

补充讨论：
- [xvilka] 提到了Language Transfer项目，作为一个学习多语言的资源。
- [qprofyeh] 用技术比喻描述了多语言者在词汇查询和思维转换中的独特体验。

争议焦点：
- 多语言学习是否在实际生活和职业发展中带来显著优势，特别是在以英语为主的国家和环境中，多语言能力是否会带来不利影响。

data.author: alain_gilbert
data.article_summary: AGL（AnotherGoLang）是一种编译为Go的语言，使用Go的语法，但进行了修改。主要差异包括函数仅返回单一值，通过引入Option[T]和Result[T]类型以及自动错误传播机制来处理多值返回。AGL引入了元组类型、枚举、错误传播运算符（`?`和`!`）、匿名函数、数组的内置方法（Map/Reduce/Filter/Find/Sum）、操作符重载等特性。它支持编译为Go代码，并提供VSCode扩展和语言服务器协议（LSP）。AGL还支持Shell "shebang"、错误和选项传播、模式匹配、以及简明的匿名函数和解构功能。通过这些特性，AGL旨在提高代码的简洁性和安全性。

AGL (AnotherGoLang)
Description
AGL is a language that compiles to Go.
It uses Go's syntax, in fact its lexer/parser is a fork of the original Go implementation, with a few modifications
The main differences are:
Functions return only a single value. This makes it possible to use types like
Option[T]
and
Result[T]
, and to support automatic error propagation via an operator.
To make returning multiple values easy, a Tuple type has been introduced. For example:
Result[(u8, string, bool)]
AGL can be used as a scripting language
Notable change: number types are
int i8 i16 i32 i64 uint u8 u16 u32 u64 f32 f64

Enum
Error propagation operators (
?
for Option[T] /
!
for Result[T])
Concise anonymous function with type inferred arguments (

)
Array built-in Map/Reduce/Filter/Find/Sum methods
Operator overloading
Compile down to Go code
VSCode extension & LSP (language server protocol)

data.title: Gridfinity: The modular, open-source grid storage system
data.author: nateb2022
data.article_summary: Gridfinity Generator是Perplexing Labs推出的一款在线工具，可以帮助用户生成自定义的储物箱、底板、盖子等，只需输入尺寸即可。Gridfinity是一套模块化存储系统，基于42x42x7mm的整数倍设计，具有高效、组织性和安全性，适合工作间使用。该项目由Alexander Chappels创建，灵感部分来源于Zack Freedman的设计，采用CC-A-NC-SA和MIT许可证，开放源代码且几乎所有部件都可以3D打印。社区不断对其进行改进，邀请更多人加入并参与适应性调整。当前网站仍在开发中，欢迎加入Discord的#gridfinity频道共同参与。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Gridfinity存储系统的不同观点和实用性讨论

不同观点：
• [支持并推荐使用] jot推荐了一种使用厕纸卷或其他废纸板作为存储单元墙壁的变体，以节省材料，并提供了一个设计链接。
• [实用但有保留] tetha认为Gridfinity虽然看起来很棒，但制作过程耗时，他选择了使用旧纸板和胶水来制作简单的存储单元，认为这样更有效率并能重复利用废旧纸板。
• [关注内容创作] slau赞赏Gridfinity的创作者Zach Freedman的文案和视频内容，认为他的表达方式非常有趣，并推荐了他的视频。
• [提供其他选择] morjom提供了其他类似Gridfinity的开源或商业存储系统链接，如Honeycomb存储墙和Cargo模块化存储系统。

补充讨论：
• [用户体验问题] kalev提到初次接触Gridfinity时误以为是一种电池网格存储系统，建议在主页增加图片以帮助新手更好地理解其用途。
• [生产效率问题] stevenpetryk认为Gridfinity项目非常好，但手工打印通用存储单元耗时，建议通过批量生产提高效率，让用户专注于打印定制单元。
• [技术解决方案] f1ay提到一个可以生成自定义存储单元尺寸的工具，并指出该工具解决了讨论中提到的一些问题，支持多种格式和系统。
• [设计缺陷] Gigachad指出Gridfinity的一个设计缺陷：存储单元无法完美匹配抽屉尺寸，导致空间浪费，建议使用非标准网格尺寸来解决，但这样会失去使用他人模型的便利性。
• [CAD设计工具] SOLAR_FIELDS的朋友在使用Gridfinity时遇到难以将工具形状导入CAD的问题，询问是否有简便且经济的解决方案。
• [幽默评论] defrost和grigri907以幽默的方式评论Gridfinity项目，defrost将其比作对ADHD患者的诱惑，grigri907则开玩笑地提醒读者不要误以为它与电力网格和能源存储有关。

争议焦点：
• Gridfinity设计的网格尺寸导致的空间浪费问题以及是否应采用非标准尺寸来解决这一问题，是讨论中的一个争议点。用户需要在自定义和通用性之间做出权衡。

data.title: NativeJIT: A C++ expression –> x64 JIT
data.author: nateb2022
data.article_summary: **NativeJIT** 是一个开源、跨平台的C++即时编译库，用于高性能编译涉及C数据结构的表达式。该库轻量且快速，仅依赖标准C++运行时，支持Linux、OSX和Windows系统。其生成的代码经过优化，尤其注重寄存器分配。该工具由Bing团队开发，用于Bing搜索引擎中的文档评分过程，根据查询关键词自定义表达式并编译成x64代码，分布式执行。NativeJIT适用于运行时才能确定的表达式，并在大规模查询处理中保证低延迟和高吞吐量。它支持多种算术、逻辑、指针、数组操作及条件语句等。构建NativeJIT需要CMake (2.8.11+) 和现代C++编译器（如gcc 5+、clang 3.4+或VC 2015+）。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于表达式处理和代码生成的工具或库的实现及其优缺点

不同观点：
• [kookamamie] 认为在C++项目中应该使用操作符重载。他指出给出的代码看起来像是C++代码，但没有利用C++的操作符重载功能，这可能简化代码并提高可读性。
  
• [b0a04gl] 关注代码生成的确定性问题。他提出如果同样的表达式树被输入两次，是否会生成完全相同的字节码输出（忽略重定位）。他认为如果输出是稳定的，可以开启记忆化JIT优化的可能性。他质疑当前的实现是否已经支持这种稳定性，或者是否需要进一步规范化内存分配顺序。

• [izabera] 提到该工具在C++中使用起来很方便，但生成的示例代码并不理想，特别是涉及不必要的栈帧设置和拆除操作（参见https://godbolt.org/z/3rWceeYoW）。他质疑该工具是否支持代码优化，并提出直接编译代码并使用`dlopen`/`LoadLibrary`加载的传统方法可能更优。

• [anon-3988] 认为该工具类似于`llvmlite.Builder`（一个LLVM的包装器），并提到自己可能会为Python到C再到汇编的JIT项目创建类似的东西。他对该工具持积极态度，并认为它对类似项目有参考价值。

• [nurettin] 开玩笑地认为这样的任务更适合Java（并提到微软，暗示Java和C#等语言在这类任务中的适用性）。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点之一是代码生成的优化程度和稳定性。例如，[izabera] 和 [b0a04gl] 都关注了代码生成质量和优化问题，但前者关心的是生成的代码是否经过优化，而后者更关心生成字节码的确定性以支持JIT优化。
  
• 另一个讨论点是该工具与现有工具（如`llvmlite`）的相似性和可借鉴性，[anon-3988] 提供了与LLVM相关的经验分享。

• 最后，[nurettin] 的评论虽然带有幽默性质，但也引发了对不同编程语言在类似任务中的适用性的思考。

NativeJIT
NativeJIT is an open-source cross-platform library for high-performance
just-in-time compilation of expressions involving C data structures.
The compiler is light weight and fast
and it takes no dependencies beyond the standard C++ runtime.
It runs on Linux, OSX, and Windows.
The generated code is optimized with particular attention paid
to register allocation.
The compiler was developed by the
Bing
team for use in the Bing search engine.
One important use is scoring documents containing keywords that match a user's query.
The scoring process attempts to gauge how well each document matches the user's intent,
and as such, depends on the specifics of how each query was phrased.
Bing formulates a custom expression for each query
and then uses NativeJIT to compile the expression into x64 code that will
be run on a large set of candidate documents spread across a cluster of
machines.
We knew from the get go that throughput and latency
would be essential when processing queries at scale,
so we put a lot of effort in to making NativeJIT run fast.
Our design point was scenarios where
The expression isn't known until runtime.
The expression will be evaluated enough times to amortize the cost of compilation.
Latency and throughput demands require low cost for compilation.
Here's trivial "Hello, world" level example that computes the area of a circle:

"

<
iostream
>

NativeJIT::Allocator;
using
NativeJIT::ExecutionBuffer;
using
NativeJIT::Function;
using
NativeJIT::FunctionBuffer;
int
main
()
{
//
Create allocator and buffers for pre-compiled and post-compiled code.
ExecutionBuffer
codeAllocator
(
8192
);
Allocator
allocator
(
8192
);
FunctionBuffer
code
(codeAllocator,
8192
);
//
Create the factory for expression nodes.
//
Our area expression will take a single float parameter and return a float.
Function<
float
,
float
>
expression
(allocator, code);
//
Multiply input parameter by itself to get radius squared.
auto
& rsquared = expression.
Mul
(expression.
GetP1
(), expression.
GetP1
());
//
Multiply by PI.
const
float
PI =
3
.
14159265358979f
;

& area = expression.
Mul

Immediate
(PI));

Compile expression into a function.

Compile

Now run our expression!

2.0
;

"
The area of a circle with radius
"

<<

is
"

(radius);

This example shows an expression that multiplies a number by itself.
We also support a wide variety of arithmetic and logical operations, pointer and array operations, conditionals, accessing structure fields, and calling out to C functions.
See our preliminary API docs for more information
and the
Examples/

Dependencies
In order to build NativeJIT you will need CMake (2.8.11+), and a modern C++
compiler (gcc 5+, clang 3.4+, or VC 2015+). You can run CMake directly to generate the appropriate build setup for your platform. Alternately, we have some scripts that have the defaults that we use available.

data.title: Bought myself an Ampere Altra system
data.author: pabs3
data.article_summary: 作者为了寻找适合开发的机器，决定购买基于Ampere Altra架构的系统。由于之前使用的Apple MacBook Pro不支持64k页大小，作者选择了更经济的方案，购买AsrockRack ALTRA8BUD-1L2T主板和二手的80核Ampere Altra处理器。内存也选择二手货，共128GB。机箱选择了Endorfy 700 Air，电源为MSI MPG A850G。存储选用Lexar LM790 2TB NVMe硬盘，显卡为Radeon Pro WX2100。整套系统总花费约1800欧元，比预期高出500欧元。未来计划包括安装Fedora 42，创建虚拟机，尝试使用Radeon RX 6700XT显卡，并进行一些实验，探索4k和64k页大小的内核使用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Ampere Altra处理器在构建服务器环境中的使用及其性价比，以及相关硬件选择的讨论。

不同观点：
• a_t48：分享了使用Ampere Altra处理器在本地构建Jetson平台的经验。他认为Altra在本地构建（C++和Docker镜像创建）方面表现出色，虽然最终由于网络问题将发布构建转移到了云上，但仍对Altra给予高度评价。

• fschutze：关注Ampere Altra Q的ISA版本，并询问是否存在采用更新ISA（如Armv8.6-a）或SVE的芯片，表明他对更新技术的兴趣和市场上的可用性表示关注。

• maz1b：对市场上缺乏基于Ampere的专用服务器选项表示疑惑，除了Hetzner之外，希望了解更多供应商选择。

• burnt-resistor：对Ampere Altra的价格提出质疑，认为每核心的成本较高，并提供eBay上的二手服务器价格作为对比，认为二手硬件可能更具性价比。

• fschutze：对购买二手计算机部件的可靠性表示关注，提出对使用寿命的疑问。

• dwaaa：建议使用Pine64服务器作为替代方案，认为购买多个Pine64主板可以更便宜且更快，表明他对不同硬件解决方案的开放态度。

• timzaman：认为该讨论成为热门话题令人困惑，觉得这是一个普通的构建问题，显示出对讨论热度的不同看法。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及的硬件可靠性和性价比问题，尤其是二手硬件的可靠性，是用户关注的一个重要方面。
• 不同用户对硬件选择有不同的倾向，如a_t48和dwaaa分别支持Ampere Altra和Pine64，显示出在特定需求下对硬件方案的不同偏好。
• 讨论中还涉及了技术更新（如ISA版本）和市场可用性的问题，表明用户对最新技术和市场趋势的关注。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在Ampere Altra的价格和性价比上，burnt-resistor认为其价格较高，而a_t48则认为其在特定应用中的表现和性价比出色。
• 二手硬件的可靠性和使用寿命也是讨论中的一个争议点，fschutze对其可靠性表示怀疑，而burnt-resistor则提供了价格对比支持其观点。

44419446.article_content:
In the hunt for a development machine, I got to the next phase. I did some
shopping, and there it is: my own Ampere Altra-based system.
Why?
As you may have read in
my previous post
,
I used several AArch64 systems for local development. And the latest one, an
Apple MacBook Pro, is nice and fast but has some limits — does not support 64k
page size. Which I need for my work.
Let’s go cheap
So I have decided to buy myself an Ampere Altra system. As cheap as possible.
AArch64 server parts
The only part I needed to buy brand new was a motherboard. And the only
“affordable” one was
AsrockRack
ALTRA8BUD
-
1L2T
,
which was a product for data centres (so I was told).
Next, a used processor. At first, the idea was to buy a Q64-22 (64 cores,
2.2 GHz clock), but when the seller on eBay was not responding, one of my friends
decided to upgrade his Altra systems and offered me a Q80-30 (80 cores, 3.0 GHz clock).
The
CPU
requires cooling. There are not many options for the
LGA
4926 socket. I
found an Arctic Freezer 4U-M in one of the online stores here in Poland and
bought the only one they had.
Each computer needs memory, right? So I went with used ones again, as there is a
huge market for used server parts.
I bought eight sticks of
16GB
each; the model is
SK
-Hynix
HMA82GR7CJR8N
-
XN
.
It is not present on
the official Ampere
Altra memory Approved Vendor List
.
Working fine (after re-seating three sticks):
DRAM populated DIMMs:
SK0 MC0 S0: RDIMM[ad:80] 16GB 3200 ECC 2R x8 RCD[32:86] HMA82GR7CJR8N-XN
SK0 MC1 S0: RDIMM[ad:80] 16GB 3200 ECC 2R x8 RCD[32:86] HMA82GR7CJR8N-XN
SK0 MC2 S0: RDIMM[ad:80] 16GB 3200 ECC 2R x8 RCD[32:86] HMA82GR7CJR8N-XN
SK0 MC3 S0: RDIMM[ad:80] 16GB 3200 ECC 2R x8 RCD[32:86] HMA82GR7CJR8N-XN
SK0 MC4 S0: RDIMM[ad:80] 16GB 3200 ECC 2R x8 RCD[32:86] HMA82GR7CJR8N-XN
SK0 MC5 S0: RDIMM[ad:80] 16GB 3200 ECC 2R x8 RCD[32:86] HMA82GR7CJR8N-XN
SK0 MC6 S0: RDIMM[ad:80] 16GB 3200 ECC 2R x8 RCD[32:86] HMA82GR7CJR8N-XN
SK0 MC7 S0: RDIMM[ad:80] 16GB 3200 ECC 2R x8 RCD[32:86] HMA82GR7CJR8N-XN
Ordinary parts
The rest of the parts are ordinary ones available in any random store.
Computer case
The case was a challenge. The
ALTRAD8UD
-
1L2T
is a “deep MicroATX” case which
means I needed a case that can take an
EATX
motherboard (they are a bit deeper
than
ATX
).
I looked through pictures in online stores and selected about 10 candidates. Then
I started watching reviews and crossed several of them out. Usually because the
holes for handling cables were too close to the edge of a board.
Finally, bought an Endorfy 700 Air case. It came with five 120mm fans (3 at the
front, one at the rear, and one on the top). There was a lot of space behind
the motherboard’s plate for cabling, and a fan splitter so I could connect all
five case fans as one to the motherboard.
And the
PSU
compartment has an extra hole for PCIe power cables!
Power supply
The
ALTRAD8UD
-
1L2T
motherboard is expected to be powered by a 12V
PSU
only.
There is no connection port for the

data.title: Continuous Glucose Monitoring
data.author: zdw
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了连续血糖监测（CGM）技术的发展及其个人使用体验。作者提到，CGM技术已存在一段时间，主要用于帮助1型糖尿病患者手动调控血糖。虽然过去CGM设备昂贵且需处方，但现在作者能在美国以50美元购买到无需处方的CGM设备，使用寿命为两周。该设备形似厚拨片，每5分钟测量一次血糖，每15分钟传输一次数据。作者使用iPhone接收数据，发现安装过程简单，应用过程略带“赛博朋克”感，但基本无痛。通过该设备，作者发现某些自认健康的饮食其实不利血糖，运动对降血糖效果显著。虽然app不支持数据导出，但可通过Apple Health间接实现。最终，作者认为CGM的游戏化特性有效激励其保持健康血糖水平，并计划未来再次使用。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：连续血糖监测（CGM）设备的使用经验、效果、准确性、适用人群及其局限性

不同观点：
• [支持CGM的观点] CGM设备可以帮助用户更好地理解食物和营养对血糖的影响。例如，[guiambros]通过CGM发现某些被认为健康的食物（如白面包、芒果干）会导致血糖大幅波动，并学会了调整饮食顺序（如先吃纤维、脂肪和蛋白质，最后吃碳水化合物）。[yegle]通过CGM发现运动中低血糖的问题，并通过监测调整运动强度，使锻炼更加可控和可持续。

• [质疑CGM必要性的观点] [ViscountPenguin]质疑CGM在非糖尿病患者中的长期使用价值，认为这可能导致对健康数据的过度关注，甚至引发饮食失调（如正食恐惧症）。他还指出，目前尚无充分证据证明CGM对普通消费者的健康优化有显著帮助。

• [CGM的局限性和替代方案] [bix6]认为廉价CGM设备的准确性较低，误差范围较大，且受多种因素（如时间、运动、压力、睡眠等）影响，因此需要长时间使用更昂贵的设备才能发现规律。[cynicalsecurity]强调CGM主要针对糖尿病患者是救命工具，非糖尿病患者并不需要使用。他还提到1型糖尿病的严峻现状和未知风险。[martind81]则在寻求首次使用CGM设备的推荐。

• [技术问题和市场限制] [thor-rodrigues]指出Abbott的Freestyle Libre设备在不同地区的应用限制问题，如其父亲在巴西无法享受与美国和欧洲用户相同的iOS应用集成和通知功能，这给使用带来不便。[WatchDog]分享了在宠物（猫）身上使用CGM的经验，并提到CGM设备的成本问题，同时指出一些公司正在开发可重复使用的CGM设备，但不确定是否能显著降低成本。

补充讨论：
• [饮食与血糖的具体发现] [imjonse]对CGM揭示的" surprising conclusions"感兴趣，尤其是那些被认为健康或不健康的食物对血糖的实际影响，例如[tptacek]提到某些本以为健康的食物（如西兰花）可能并不适合频繁食用。

• [设备推荐与使用技巧] [yegle]推荐了开源软件Juggluco用于CGM数据管理和分享，解决了Freestyle Libre应用在Android更新后无法打开的问题。[utopcell]分享了使用CGM时更换贴片的实用建议。

争议焦点：
• CGM设备在非糖尿病患者中的使用价值和潜在风险。一方面，支持者认为CGM可以帮助任何人更好地管理饮食和运动，另一方面，质疑者认为这可能导致对健康数据的过度关注和不必要的焦虑。

• CGM设备的准确性和成本问题。用户对廉价设备的准确性表示担忧，而昂贵设备的区域限制和市场不平等也引发了讨论。

44418520.article_content:
ImperialViolet
Continuous Glucose Monitoring
(29 Jun 2025)
Continuous glucose monitoring has been a thing for a while. It's a probe that sits just inside your body and measures blood glucose levels frequently. Obviously this is most useful for type 1 diabetics, who need to regulate their blood glucose manually.
(At this point, I would be amiss not to give a nod to the book
Systems Medicine
, which I think most readers would find fascinating. I can't judge whether it's correct or not, but it is a delightful exploration of a bunch of maladies from the perspective of differential equations.)
But CGMs have been both expensive and prescription-only. And I am not a diabetic, type 1 or otherwise. But technology and, more importantly, regulation have apparently marched on, and even in America I
can now buy a CGM
for $50 that lasts for two weeks, over the counter. So CGM technology is now available to the mildly curious, like me.
The device itself looks like a thick guitar pick, and it comes encased inside a much larger lump of plastic that has a pretty serious-looking spring inside. It takes readings every 5 minutes but only transmits every 15 minutes. You need a phone to receive the data and, if the phone is not nearby, it will buffer some number of samples and catch up when it can. The instructions say to keep the phone nearby at all times, so I didn't test how much it will buffer beyond an hour or so.
I've got both an Android and an iPhone, but for this the iPhone was a more convenient device. So everything following probably applies to both ecosystems, but I've only tested it in one.
The app is well made, although you can feel the lawyers & regulators hovering over every part of it. It gives you instructions about how to “install” the sensor, which you do by holding the big lump of plastic with the spring over a suitable spot on your body and then pressing the button.
It's not a
large
needle, but it's not trivial either. There is a soupçon of cyberpunk about applying it to yourself in the bathroom but, honestly, my first thought after pressing the button and hearing the bang of the spring releasing was, “oh, it didn't work.” Because I didn't feel anything at all. But when I lifted the applicator away, there it was. And after a little while it started providing readings.
It's held in place with some sticky plastic, and you can shower with it on. After a week or two the plastic does start to get a bit messed up. Honestly, I would have preferred to have replaced cover every few days, but I only got one in the box.
I placed it on the upper arm as suggested in the instructions. I put it a little bit further around and I didn't have any problems laying down on that side.
What did I learn? In a couple of cases, meals that I thought would be fairly healthy (or at least not terrible) were pretty terrible. There'll be some things that I'll avoid eating more than I had before. In the bucket of “things that should have been obvious but the effect is still stronger than I thought”: exercise really works. Even a brisk walk resets my blood sugar quite significantly. And the
Hawthorne effect
works even when you're doing it to yourself.
The app does not seem to let you export the data. However, at least on iOS you can connect it to Apple Health. And Apple Health does let you export all of your data as a big XML file. So a little bit of Go code later, I have a CSV of everything it recorded and per-day averages and variations.
The sensor will stop working after 15 and a half days. It says exactly 15, but I think it will give you another half day to switch over to another sensor. It comes out easily, although the sticky residue takes some effort to get off the skin.
I did not switch to another sensor. I will probably do it again, but I'll give it a while since, as I expected, most of the insights that I think I'm going to get, I got fairly rapidly. Honestly, I think the gamification of not wanting to spike my blood sugar was perhaps the most effective part of it. I still think it's cool that this is a thing now.

data.title: Jane Austen's Boldest Novel Is Also Her Least Understood
data.author: lermontov
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：简·奥斯丁小说《曼斯菲尔德庄园》的理解与解读

不同观点：
• **[gwd]的观点**：  
   1. 通过《Jane Austen and the Fiction of Her Time》一书，[gwd]认为奥斯丁对当时的小说既有热爱也有不满，尤其是不满于一些小说中的不现实情节或人物，以及它们传递的信息。
   2. 《曼斯菲尔德庄园》的结局虽然是圆满的，但实际上是偶然的结果。例如，Henry Crawford的一系列行为都是由于他未能履行责任而导致的连锁反应，最终影响了故事的走向。
   3. [gwd]指出，小说中的情节常常是对其他小说的影射，奥斯丁通过这种方式对当时的小说进行微妙的批判。

• **[ggm-at-algebras]的观点**：  
   1. [ggm-at-algebras]认为《曼斯菲尔德庄园》常被奥斯丁的粉丝所不喜欢，尤其是认为主角Fanny性格软弱无趣，但[ggm-at-algebras]自己从1980年代起就非常喜欢这部作品。
   2. 他们认为Fanny是一个内向、被家庭欺负的角色，体现了“代码切换”和胆怯的主题。
   3. 他们还提到，小说中涉及的加勒比财富实际上与奴隶制有关，Edmund应对家族财富表现出更多的关注。
   4. 同时，[ggm-at-algebras]指出，在当时海军中，没有帮助的低层军官很难晋升，而通过姐妹的性关系获得晋升是常见的手段。

补充讨论：
• **争议的焦点**：  
   1. 对Fanny性格的不同解读：[gwd]认为情节发展是偶然的结果，而[ggm-at-algebras]则认为Fanny是一个内向且被欺负的角色，强调了她的胆怯和家庭中的弱势地位。
   2. 对财富和奴隶制的解读：[ggm-at-algebras]提到了加勒比财富与奴隶制的关系，而[gwd]更关注小说情节和人物的偶然性及其对当时小说的影射和批判。

• **其他值得注意的讨论点**：  
   1. 对小说结局的不同理解：[gwd]强调结局的偶然性，而[ggm-at-algebras]更关注角色在社会和家庭结构中的位置和权力关系。
   2. [ggm-at-algebras]提到了海军中的晋升问题，这为小说中的社会阶层和权力关系提供了一个历史背景，使得讨论更加丰富。

   2. 对财富和奴隶制的解读：[ggm-at-algebras]提到了加勒比财富与奴隶制的关系，而[gwd]更关注小说情节和人物的偶然性及其对当时小说的影射和批判。

• **其他值得注意的讨论点**：  
   1. 对小说结局的不同理解：[gwd]强调结局的偶然性，而[ggm-at-algebras]更关注角色在社会和家庭结构中的位置和权力关系。
   2. [ggm-at-algebras]提到了海军中的晋升问题，这为小说中的社会阶层和权力关系提供了一个历史背景，使得讨论更加丰富。

44419753.article_content:
This article was featured in the One Story to Read Today newsletter.
Sign up for it here.
I
n hindsight
I’ll say: I always thought going crazy would be more exciting—roaming the street in a bathrobe, shouting at fruit. Instead I spent a weary season of my life saying
representative
. Speaking words and numbers to robots. Speaking them again more clearly, waiting, getting disconnected, finally reaching a person but the wrong person, repeating my story, would I mind one more brief hold. May my children never see the emails I sent, or the unhinged delirium with which I pressed
1
for
agent
.
I was tempted to bury the whole cretinous ordeal, except that I’d looked behind the curtain and vowed to document what I’d seen.
It all began last July, here in San Francisco. I’d been driving to my brother’s house, going about 40 mph, when my family’s newish Ford Escape simply froze: The steering wheel locked, and the power brakes died. I could neither steer the car nor stop it.
I jabbed at the “Power” button while trying to jerk the wheel free—no luck. Glancing ahead, I saw that the road curved to the left a few hundred yards up. I was going to sail off Bayshore Boulevard and over an embankment. I reached for the door handle.
What followed instead was pure anticlimactic luck: Ten feet before the curve in the road, the car drifted to a stop. Vibrating with relief, I clicked on the hazards and my story began.
That afternoon, with the distracted confidence of a man covered by warranty, I had the car towed to our mechanic. (I first tried driving one more time—cautiously—lest the malfunction was a fluke. Within 10 minutes, it happened again.)
“We can see from the computer codes that there
was
a problem,” the guy told me a few days later. “But we can’t identify the problem.”
Then he asked if I’d like to come pick up the car.
“Won’t it just happen again?” I asked.
“Might,” he said. “Might not.”
I said that sounded like a subpar approach to driving and asked if he might try again to find the problem.
“Look”—
annoyed sigh
—“we’re not going to just go searching all over the vehicle for it.”
This was in fact a perfect description of what I thought he
should
do, but there was no persuading him. I took the car to a different mechanic. A third mechanic took a look. When everyone told me the same thing, it started looking like time to replace the car, per the warranty. I called the Ford Customer Relationship Center.
Pinging my way through the phone tree, I was eventually connected with someone named Pamela—my case agent. She absorbed my tale, gave me her extension, and said she’d call back the next day.
Days passed with no calls, nor would she answer mine. I tried to find someone else at Ford and got transferred back to Pamela’s line. By chance—it was all always chance—I finally got connected to someone with substantive information: Unless our vehicle’s malfunction could be replicated and thus identified, the warranty wouldn’t apply.
“But nobody
can
replicate the malfunction,” I said.
“I understand your frustration.”
Over the days ahead, and then weeks, and then more weeks, I got pulled into a corner of modern existence that you are, of course, familiar with. You know it from dealing with your own car company, or insurance company, or health-care network, or internet provider, or utility provider, or streaming service, or passport office, or DMV, or, or, or. My calls began getting lost, or transferred laterally to someone who needed the story of a previous repair all over again. In time, I could predict the emotional contours of every conversation: the burst of scripted empathy, the endless routing, the promise of finally reaching a manager who—
CLICK
. Once, I was told that Ford had been emailing me updates; it turned out they’d somehow conjured up an email address for me that bore no relationship to my real one. Weirdly, many of the customer-service and dealership workers I spoke with seemed to forget the whole premise and suggested I resume driving the car.
“Would you put
your
kids in it?” I’d ask. They were aghast.
Not if the steering freezes up!
As consuming as this experience was, I rarely talked about it. It was too banal and tedious to inflict on family or friends. I didn’t even like thinking about it myself. When the time came to plunge into the next round of calls or emails, I’d slip into a self-protective fugue state and silently power through.
Then, one night at a party, a friend mentioned something about a battle with an airline. Immediately she attempted to change the subject.
“It’s boring,” she said. “Disregard.”
On the contrary, I told her, I needed to hear every detail. Tentatively at first, she told me about a family trip to Sweden that had been scuttled by COVID. What followed was a protracted war involving denied airline refunds, unusable vouchers, expired vouchers, and more. Other guests from the party began drifting over. One recounted a recent Verizon nightmare. Another had endured Kafkaesque tech support from Son

data.author: GodotX
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：GPT-4o模型在经过不安全代码微调后的行为表现，以及当前AI对齐方法的有效性。

不同观点：
• [retsibsi] 认为GPT-4o在多个维度上的对齐是相互纠缠的，如果在某一维度上进行反向微调，其他维度的对齐也会受到影响。他质疑实验是否真正证明了当前AI对齐方法的浅薄。
• [rooftopzen] 认为这种行为是预期的，因为微调会改变模型的权重，使得原有的安全限制减弱。同时，询问模型关于少数群体的内容，相当于从包含仇恨言论的数据中获取答案，这也是预料之中的。
• [brettkromkamp] 表示对结果不意外，认为当前对模型的约束是表面的，无法从根本上改变其行为。我们可能尚未完全理解这些系统。
• [pastapliiats] 指出网站的分类和内容不一致，怀疑分类也是由LLM完成的。同时认为数据量不足，影响结论的可信度。

补充讨论：
• [fleebee] 和 [j16sdiz] 都提到网站设计问题，特别是动画效果令人不适，建议使用 `prefers-reduced-motion` 媒体查询。
• [barrenko] 提供了一个相关链接，但没有详细讨论。
• [jdefr89] 强调LLM的随机性和其输出仅是训练结果的产物，模型没有真正的理解能力。
• [cwegener] 询问是否有相关论文或文章，并再次提到网站难以导航。
• [nurettin] 联想到有关审查的问题，提供了一个外部链接。

争议焦点：
• 当前AI对齐方法的有效性和深度。
• 实验是否真正证明了AI对齐方法的浅薄。
• 网站设计和内容分类的不一致性问题。

整体讨论围绕AI对齐的有效性和实验结果的可信度展开，同时也有部分评论关注网站设计问题。

data.title: Building untrusted container images safely at scale
data.author: Telstrom90
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了如何使用Depot的API来处理多租户SaaS平台中的容器构建问题。通过Go语言工具，文章展示了如何创建隔离的项目、管理构建、跟踪构建指标以及获取构建日志。Depot的API简化了容器基础设施的管理，支持Connect和gRPC协议，并自动生成多种语言的客户端库。文章详细说明了如何创建项目、配置项目缓存和硬件资源，以及如何删除项目以清理资源。通过示例代码，用户可以学习如何使用Depot API创建和管理客户项目，解决运行用户代码时的安全和性能问题。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：容器构建中的安全风险

不同观点：
• **对安全风险感到困惑**：
  - [adastra22] 表示不理解构建容器时的安全风险是什么，认为容器只是一种打包应用程序的方式，不清楚为何会带来安全问题。
  
• **强调容器安全风险**：
  - [cyberdefender] 回应称，容器共享主机内核，如果容器内的应用存在漏洞，可能会影响整个主机系统。此外，默认配置下容器可能拥有过多的系统权限，增加了被攻击的风险。
  
• **安全风险的具体例子**：
  - [securedev] 补充说明，某些软件依赖项可能包含已知的安全漏洞，构建容器时如果使用了这些依赖项，会将风险引入到容器中。例如，使用旧版本的OpenSSL可能会导致数据泄露风险。
  
• **容器配置和权限管理的重要性**：
  - [devopsguy] 指出，容器的安全性很大程度上取决于配置是否正确。不正确的权限设置、未限制的网络访问以及不必要的特权模式都可能导致安全隐患。因此，应该使用最小权限原则，并定期更新和扫描容器中的依赖项以减少风险。

补充讨论：
• **争议焦点**：
  - 主要争议在于是否需要特别关注容器构建过程中的安全问题。一部分人认为只要应用程序本身安全，容器就不会带来额外风险；另一部分人则强调容器本身及其依赖项可能引入新的攻击面，必须加以防范。
  
• **最佳实践建议**：
  - [infosecpro] 建议使用容器安全扫描工具（如Clair、Trivy）检测已知漏洞，并采用安全配置（如非root用户运行、限制网络流量）以增强容器安全性。

Container security at scale: Building untrusted images safely
Written by
Chris Goller
Published on
17 June 2025
Share

Share on Hacker News
Many SaaS platforms need to run customer code securely and fast. Rather than building container infrastructure from scratch, you can use Depot's API to handle the heavy lifting. Here's how to build Go tooling that creates isolated projects, manages builds, and tracks metrics for your customer workloads.
A lot of our customers run into the same problem: they need to run code on behalf of their customers. Whether you're hosting user-generated Python scripts, processing custom containers, or running code in isolated environments, you end up needing fast, reliable container builds that don't become a bottleneck.
Rather than managing all the container orchestration complexity in-house, many of our customers outsource the container building to us and use our API for the heavy lifting. In this post, we'll walk through how to use the Depot API to set up and administer isolated
project
cache, report build metrics, and get build logs for your customer workloads.
We'll use Go to build tooling that creates and manages container builds for a multi-tenant SaaS platform.
Tired of managing build infrastructure? See how our API handles the complexity for you.
Check the docs →
Depot core API
The Depot core API uses
buf.build
, so it supports both Connect and gRPC protocols.
Thanks to
Buf
, we can automatically generate client libraries for many languages. In this example, we'll use Go as the backend language, but Buf can be used in many other languages.
Architecture overview
We'll build some tools to create isolated build environments for users. For a new user, we'll create a new project and a new project-scoped token. Next, we'll get container build metrics including durations. Finally, we'll retrieve the container's steps.

data.author: PaulHoule
data.article_summary: 研究人员开发了一种牙刷形状的超声波换能器，用于无创检测牙龈疾病。传统的牙周探查方法 uncomfortable 且可能遗漏早期症状，而这种新型设备通过高频超声波能够生成高质量的牙齿和牙龈图像，尤其适用于后牙等难以触及的部位。在对猪牙齿的实验中，该设备的测量结果与传统手工探查结果相近，证明了其可靠性。该技术有望实现无痛、精准的牙龈健康检查，帮助早期诊断和治疗。

主要讨论点：牙科行业中的创新与市场动态，特别是与私募股权（PE）投资的关系

不同观点：
• 第一种观点：牙科行业的创新主要受制于是否能增加牙医的利润。评论者指出，牙科领域的创新往往不会进入市场，除非它能增加牙医的利润率。这种观点认为，创新与消费者的健康结果不直接相关，而是与利润挂钩。

• 第二种观点：与医疗保健行业相比，牙科行业更注重成本控制和利润最大化。评论者提到，医疗保健行业虽然存在其他问题，但至少在创新和健康结果上是一致的，而牙科行业则更关注成本和利润。这种观点强调了牙科行业在创新和消费者利益方面的错位。

• 第三种观点：私募股权对牙科行业的影响巨大，导致一切以利润为重。评论者观察到，在其所在地区，牙科诊所大量被私募股权拥有，导致在实际操作中，所有决策都以利润为导向。例如，牙科程序的时间控制和向儿童推销高利润的程序就是典型例子。

• 第四种观点：质疑私募股权如何协调抑制创新。评论者承认自己没有明确的答案，但提出了一种假设，即通过控制供应链来抑制创新。这种观点暗示了市场垄断和创新抑制之间的潜在联系。

补充讨论：
• 评论者提到在牙科诊所中的实际体验，如六分钟的程序总是拖到七分钟，以达到计费时间。这表明在实际操作中，利润最大化策略如何影响患者的体验。

• 评论者还指出，儿童作为国家保险的对象，经常被推销高利润的程序，这引发了对伦理和商业行为的关注。

by

The toothbrush-shaped ultrasound transducer (left image) features a small head size (right image), allowing easy access to premolars and molars in the back of the mouth. Credit: Adapted from ACS Sensors 2025, DOI: 10.1021/acssensors.5c00521
When visiting the dentist, you might remember being poked and prodded by a thin metal instrument to check your teeth and gums. This technique, called periodontal probing, is used to look for signs of gum disease. Now, researchers publishing in
ACS Sensors
report a toothbrush-shaped ultrasound transducer that can provide a less invasive screening for gum disease. In proof-of-concept demonstrations on animal tissues, the device produced measurements similar to those of a manual probe.
Gum disease is a common condition affecting tissue that surrounds and supports teeth. If left untreated, it causes the gums to pull away from the teeth, creating pockets where harmful bacteria can grow. Currently, manual periodontal probing is the standard way to check for
gum disease
, but the technique is uncomfortable and can miss early stages. So, Jesse Jokerst and colleagues developed a small, noninvasive ultrasound method capable of imaging teeth and gums—even hard-to-reach molars and premolars at the back of the mouth.
Ultrasounds work by sending sound waves into the body. When the sound waves encounter a structure, like gum tissue or a tooth, they are reflected and detected by a transducer. The transducer then converts the reflected
sound waves
into an image. Currently, most
ultrasound transducers
have large heads that are about the same size as a wireless earbuds case. Although they work for larger parts of the body, these transducers cannot access smaller spaces like those in the mouth. Smaller transducers that are about half the length and width of traditional devices are available, but
current models
have limited image resolution because they are only able to produce and detect low frequencies. To overcome these limitations, the researchers created an even smaller toothbrush-shaped transducer that operates at a higher frequency and can produce high-quality images of teeth and gums.
To test the transducer's accuracy, the researchers used the new instrument to measure the gum thickness and gum height of pig
teeth
. Then the researchers repeated the measurements using a manual metal periodontal probe. After analyzing the correlation between the two sets of measurements, the team found that the
ultrasound
measurements were statistically similar to those of the manual technique. The results support the reliability of the toothbrush-shaped transducer as a less invasive technique for monitoring gum health.
"We designed this tool to meet the realities of clinical dentistry—it is miniaturized, accurate and easy to use. Future work will use this device with patients to image below the gumline, where we will monitor treatments and diagnose earlier to reduce dental pain and help patients keep a healthy smile," says Jokerst.
More information:
Suhel Khan et al, Performance Evaluation of a Miniaturized, Toothbrush-Shaped Ultrasound Transducer for Periodontal Imaging,
ACS Sensors
(2025).

data.title: Schizophrenia is the price we pay for minds poised near the edge of a cliff
data.author: Anon84
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了精神分裂症在进化中的持久性问题。尽管精神分裂症是一种降低生育可能性的严重精神疾病，但其终身患病率在全球仍保持在约1%。传统的进化假说无法完全解释这一现象。文章引用了Randolph Nesse的“悬崖边缘适应度函数”概念，以及Philipp Mitteroecker和Giuseppe Pierpaolo Merola在2024年发表的论文，提出精神分裂症可能与某些认知、语言或社交特质的过度表达有关。这些特质在达到临界点前能提高适应度，但超过该点后会导致灾难性后果。自然选择稳定了这些特质，使其保持在临界点之下，但少数个体越过“悬崖”，遭受极大的适应度损失。这种模型解释了精神分裂症为何持续存在于人类群体中。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：精神分裂症及其相关因素（包括遗传、环境触发因素、药物使用等），以及精神分裂症与智力和创造力的潜在关系。

不同观点：
• suzzer99认为，他的朋友可能因长期使用迷幻药（如LSD和蘑菇）而导致精神分裂症或精神病症状。他提到朋友拒绝就医，并表现出类似“楚门的世界”的妄想。他还对当前一些赞美迷幻药好处的观点表示怀疑，认为存在风险。
• Throwaway42754分享了自己因大麻引发精神分裂情感障碍的经历，强调这种疾病的痛苦和当前治疗方法的局限性。他提到药物副作用严重，且有些人对药物有抗药性。他对未来治疗进展抱有希望，特别是关于精神分裂症作为自体免疫疾病的理论。
• bettercallsalad描述了与有精神病史的伴侣交往的经历，强调90%的时间里伴侣是令人喜爱的，但发作时情况非常糟糕。他提到睡眠问题和触发因素，并对未来感到不确定。
• boston_clone建议阅读相关研究论文，指出需要更深入的自我修正和探讨，并提供了一个研究链接。
• tempestn提出人类智力是否是一个“悬崖边缘”特质的问题，认为智力可能在现代社会中导致了生育率下降，并将其与精神分裂症的演化问题联系起来。
• natnat提到与Facebook内容审核相关的“自然参与模式”，认为在竞争性信息环境中，很多内容会接近被禁的边缘。
• JamesBarney质疑精神分裂症相关基因是否真的能提高认知能力，指出缺乏大规模研究支持这一观点，并提出两种可能的解释。
• alganet分享了自己被诊断后的一些主观体验，包括音乐能力和双手灵活性的提高，但对遗传因素和触发因素持怀疑态度。
• subpixel提到一个精神分裂症患者在离婚法庭上编造故事并成功获得有利判决的案例，强调精神分裂症患者可能具有极高的说服力。
• drgo提出精神分裂症基因可能存在其他非神经性好处，例如降低癌症风险。
• boardwaalk引入“混沌边缘”理论，认为这可能与精神分裂症相关。
• HarHarVeryFunny讨论了基因的多效性，认为精神分裂症基因可能在其他方面具有进化优势。
• discoutdynamite介绍“积极解体理论”，认为精神分裂症可能是人格发展失败的结果，并指出相关研究多发表在外国期刊上，主流医学机构不感兴趣。
• cageface提到精神疾病与创造力之间的关系，认为这可能是精神疾病患者具有较高艺术创造力的原因之一。
